findings.issue: A few figures restate across subsections of the same section, flagged by the figure-repeat-unit lint as non-blocking warnings: the current price $261.28 recurs in valuation and finalRecommendation; 49.6x and 9.8% recur in scenarioCommentary after multiplesCommentary; the Class A share count 254,580,533 recurs in governance and insiderOwnership; $5.84B ARR and 51% recur across the moat and growth sections. None is a wrong or ungrounded figure -- the build's grounding check passed with zero ungrounded figures -- and each is introduced correctly in its home; the repeats are stylistic.
findings.fix: In a future pass, refer back in words at the second mention (e.g., 'today's price', 'that multiple', 'the shares outstanding noted above') rather than restating the figure.
findings.note: scenarioCommentary now says 'about 2% below the current price' and drops 49.6x and 9.8%; finalRecommendation states $261.28 once; insiderOwnership refers to 'the Class A share count above'; moatFactors[1] says 'The ARR base above'; growth.points[3] says 'a majority'. Cross-section paraphrase repetition is raised separately in F-8 and F-9.

findings.quote: The vendor's snapshot labels the July quarter as 'Q3 2026'; we use the company's own label, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, throughout.
findings.issue: Verification note, not a defect: the two known data traps are handled correctly. The vendor's non-Dec-FYE quarter mislabel ('Q3 2026') is flagged once and the company's Q2 FY2027 label is used throughout. The pack's share-count and market-cap figures are internally inconsistent (market cap implies ~1.02B shares while the proxy reports 254,580,533 Class A shares outstanding); the report does not state an absolute share count in the prose, grounds valuation in the given multiples and ownership in the proxy, so no contradiction reaches the reader. Calls math checks out: weighted FV ~$255, E -2.2%, D -29.2%, derived HOLD, band $220-$305 brackets Base $255, Bear $185 is 29% below price.
findings.fix: No change required. A fresh independent reviewer should re-verify when the subagent runner recovers, given this was an inline self-review.
findings.note: Re-verified independently. Quarter label still handled once. The share-basis gap is now disclosed in incomeCommentary and insiderOwnership, and the report says it does not compare the series (but see F-7, where two risk bullets do). Calls: E -2.2%, D -29.2%, derived HOLD, band $220-$305 brackets the Base $245; the stated SELL and BUY flip directions match the page's math.

findings.quote: Falcon Flex ending ARR surpassed $2.29 billion, up 101% year-over-year, evidence that customers are consolidating security spend onto the platform
findings.issue: Wrong quantity. The press release says the company 'Exceeds $2.29 billion in ending ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex' -- the total ARR of Flex-adopting accounts, not ARR booked under Falcon Flex. The report relabels it as 'Falcon Flex ending ARR' / 'Falcon Flex ARR' in five places: analystCommentary ('Falcon Flex ending ARR exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101%'), executiveSummary.thesis.body ('Falcon Flex ARR above $2.29 billion growing 101%'), executiveSummary.catalysts[1] ('ending Falcon Flex ARR extended its rapid year-over-year climb'), businessMoat.moatFactors[2] and growth.points[1]. The relabel overstates how much spend runs through the Flex model, which is the evidence the moat factor and the catalyst rest on.
findings.fix: Everywhere the figure appears, attach it to its own subject: ending ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101%. Draw only the conclusion that subject supports (accounts on Flex are growing their total ARR quickly), not that spend under Flex itself is that size.

findings.quote: Consensus sees revenue reaching about $6 billion in fiscal 2027 and $7.4 billion in fiscal 2028, with EPS of $1.26 and $1.61, though annual growth continues to decelerate as the base scales.
findings.issue: The surface contradicts 'continues to decelerate'. The Facts block gives FY26 revenue growth of +21.7% and FY27E revenue growth of +25%, so consensus has annual growth re-accelerating in fiscal 2027, not continuing to slow. The latest quarter points the same way: second-quarter revenue rose 26%, and ARR growth was 25% at July 31, 2026 against 20% a year earlier (MD&A ARR table). A statement the page's own figures refute is an unsupported claim.
findings.fix: Say what the surface shows: consensus has fiscal 2027 growth above fiscal 2026's +21.7% (the Facts give +25%), and the fiscal 2028 revenue figure implies a further step; describe any later slowing in words without computing a new rate. Drop 'continues to decelerate'.

findings.quote: Growth deceleration: annual revenue growth has slowed from 54.4% in fiscal 2023 to 21.7% in fiscal 2026
findings.issue: Two problems. (1) Repetition: the annual-deceleration claim is made in five places -- executiveSummary.risks[3], financials.incomeCommentary ('the picture is growth decelerating as the base scales ... easing from 54.4% to 21.7%'), risks.idiosyncratic[2] ('annual revenue growth has decelerated each year as the base has scaled'), businessMoat.durability ('annual revenue growth has already slowed markedly since fiscal 2023') and finalRecommendation.body[1] ('a deceleration in annual revenue growth since fiscal 2023'). (2) Counter-case: none of them gives the reading that cuts the other way, though it is on the page -- second-quarter revenue +26% against FY26 +21.7%, ARR growth 25% against 20% a year earlier, net new ARR growth 51%, and FY27E revenue +25%. The report uses that re-acceleration only to argue the Bull weight, so the deceleration story reads as settled when the latest data run against it.
findings.fix: Argue growth once, in incomeCommentary: the fiscal-year series slowed through fiscal 2026, then the second quarter, ARR growth and the FY27 consensus turned up; say which the report weighs more and why. Elsewhere point back in words (e.g. 'the growth path discussed under financials'), and keep the exec-summary risk a one-line pointer.

findings.quote: but the same team presided over the July 19, 2024 Incident and the customer-commitment discounting that followed
findings.issue: Recalled tenure. The surface names George Kurtz as Founder and Chief Executive Officer and Burt Podbere as Chief Financial Officer only as of the August 26, 2026 press release (and lists both in the April 3, 2026 proxy ownership table without titles or start dates). Nothing on the surface says either held his role in July 2024, so 'the same team presided over' the incident is a tenure claim from memory.
findings.fix: Remove the tenure claim. If the point is that execution risk is real, make it from the incident and the revision themselves without saying who was in office, e.g. 'the July 19, 2024 Incident and the revision of prior-year interim figures are reminders that execution risk is real'.

findings.quote: GAAP profitability: GAAP results are near breakeven (second-quarter diluted EPS $0.01; fiscal 2026 diluted EPS -$0.65)
findings.issue: Cross-basis comparison the report itself rules out. incomeCommentary says the annual per-share series 'appears to sit on a much smaller share count than the quarterly, consensus and guidance figures ... so we do not compare the two series'. Yet executiveSummary.risks[2] and risks.idiosyncratic[3] ('fiscal 2026 diluted EPS -$0.65; second-quarter $0.01') set the annual EPS beside the quarterly EPS in one parenthesis as evidence of the same point. A reader takes -$0.65 and $0.01 as comparable per-share figures, which on the report's own reading they are not; the annual loss per share looks far larger next to the quarter than it would on one basis.
findings.fix: In both bullets, make the near-breakeven point on figures with no share-basis issue -- fiscal 2026 net income of -$162.5M or the FY26 operating margin of -6.1%, and the quarter's GAAP net income of $5.3 million -- or keep one EPS figure only. Do not place the annual and quarterly EPS side by side.

findings.quote: AI-security demand: new offerings such as Continuous Identity for AI Agents and Falcon AIDR, plus alliances with AWS, Cerebras and Schwarz Digits, extend the platform into securing AI workloads.
findings.issue: Executive-summary pointers are near-verbatim copies of the section bullets behind them, so the section does not argue anything the summary did not already say: (a) catalysts[4] vs growth.points[5] ('offerings such as Continuous Identity for AI Agents and Falcon AIDR, and alliances with AWS, Cerebras and Schwarz Digits, target securing enterprise AI workloads'); (b) catalysts[0] vs growth.points[2] (both: raised FY27 net new ARR growth outlook by 630 basis points to 34% at the midpoint, plus the $5,991.1-$6,011.1 million revenue guide, which companyOverview also states); (c) catalysts[1] ('pulling broader, larger platform commitments') vs growth.points[1] ('pulls larger, broader platform commitments'); (d) risks[2] vs risks.idiosyncratic[3] (both: GAAP near breakeven, the same two EPS figures, so the shareholder relies on ARR/free cash flow), with thesis.body making the same point a third time; (e) the consensus revenue path ($4.8B to about $6B to $7.4B) appears in both valuation.multiplesCommentary and growth.points[4].
findings.fix: Keep each catalyst and risk to a one-line pointer with no more than one figure; let the growth bullets and idiosyncratic risks carry the figures and the mechanism (what to watch, what would change the view). State the revenue guide once (growth or overview, not both plus a catalyst), and the consensus revenue path once (valuation or growth).

findings.quote: at 49.6x sales the equity is valued for years of ARR growth near today's pace and for margin expansion
findings.issue: Paraphrase repetition across sections. (a) The valuation argument -- 49.6x sales, priced for years of growth near today's pace plus margin expansion -- is made in thesis.body, valuation.multiplesCommentary, businessMoat.durability and risks.idiosyncratic[1] (which restates 49.6x, 208.0x, $235.67 and 162.7x). (b) The July 19 mechanism (elongated sales cycles, competitor approaches, commitment discounting raising contraction) is argued in both durability and risks.idiosyncratic[0]. (c) 'Net cash lets management invest, acquire and buy back' is made in balanceCommentary, management.capitalAllocation and catalysts[3] ('future buyback capacity'). (d) Stock-based-compensation dilution is argued in cashflowCommentary, capitalAllocation, risks.idiosyncratic[3] and finalRecommendation.body[2]. (e) The immaterial-error revision is told in incomeCommentary and leadership. (f) The 51%/35%/26% module-adoption figures appear in both companyOverview and moatFactors[0].
findings.fix: Give each claim one home and point back in words elsewhere: valuation in valuation (durability and risks.idiosyncratic[1] say 'the multiple discussed under valuation'); the incident mechanism in risks.idiosyncratic[0]; capital capacity in capitalAllocation; SBC dilution in one place; the revision once; the module figures in the moat factor (overview can say 'a rising share of customers run six or more modules').

findings.quote: an assumed 115x the same fiscal 2028 consensus EPS, a little over half today's current-year multiple, for a market that stops paying a growth premium, gives about $185
findings.issue: The stated basis does not describe the multiple. 115x a year-out consensus EPS is still a very large growth premium, so 'a market that stops paying a growth premium' misstates what the Bear assumes; a reader checking the basis finds the words and the number pointing in opposite directions. The only anchor is 'a little over half today's' multiple, a fraction of the price-dependent figure rather than anything independent on the surface (the Street's low target and consensus target are on the page). The Bear's 25% weight is argued in scenarioCommentary, but the price it weights is not.
findings.fix: Either re-describe the multiple honestly (a partial de-rating that still leaves a growth premium) and argue why that, rather than a deeper de-rating, is the downside case, or anchor the Bear to a checkable surface figure and say why it is the right one. Re-derive the label from whatever Bear you settle on and let the rule decide it.

findings.quote: The land-and-expand model and the Falcon Flex licensing framework let customers commit broadly upfront and draw down across products
findings.issue: No counter-case for Falcon Flex, though one is on the page. The MD&A warns that 'if our customers are not able to fully utilize their product subscriptions (including in connection with our flexible subscription offering), we may experience increased contraction as such customers may elect to renew with shorter subscription periods, fewer cloud modules, fewer endpoints or smaller contract values'. The report treats Flex as purely bullish in catalysts[1], moatFactors[2] and growth.points[1]. risks.idiosyncratic[2] paraphrases the same MD&A sentence but drops its condition (customers not fully using what they bought, including under the flexible offering), so the link to Flex is lost.
findings.fix: In the moat factor, add the bear sentence in the company's words: commitments drawn down over time can turn into contraction at renewal if customers do not use them, and the company names its flexible subscription offering in that warning. In risks.idiosyncratic[2], keep the condition the MD&A attaches. Do not equate the 'flexible subscription offering' with Falcon Flex beyond what the text says.

findings.quote: Competition is intense, and pricing is disciplined by rivals rather than by CrowdStrike alone.
findings.issue: Unsupported inference. The 10-K risk factors say the company faces intense competition and that certain competitors aggressively approached customers and partners after the July 19 Incident. No source says rivals discipline CrowdStrike's pricing; the only discounting on the surface is the company's own customer-commitment packages tied to the incident. The sentence states as fact an inference the source invites but does not make.
findings.fix: Keep what the source says (intense competition; competitors approached customers and partners after the incident) and drop the pricing claim, or frame it explicitly as the report's own judgment rather than a finding.

findings.quote: AI security is an emerging vector: offerings such as Continuous Identity for AI Agents and Falcon AIDR, and alliances with AWS, Cerebras and Schwarz Digits, target securing enterprise AI workloads.
findings.issue: Over-attribution, here and in executiveSummary.catalysts[4]. The press release describes the Schwarz Digits partnership as 'a multi-year roadmap to bring the AI-native Falcon platform to European enterprises' plus the agreed XM Cyber asset purchase (attack path visualization and offensive simulation) -- not an alliance aimed at securing AI workloads. Falcon AIDR is also not a new offering on the surface: the release says the company 'Extended' it across AI gateway partners, while catalysts[4] calls it one of the 'new offerings'.
findings.fix: Keep AWS (AI, cloud and Next-Gen SIEM innovations to help build and operate AI applications) and Cerebras (AI inference at scale) as the AI-security alliances; describe Schwarz Digits by what the release says it is (European distribution roadmap and the XM Cyber assets). Say Falcon AIDR was extended to more AI gateway partners rather than calling it new.

findings.quote: and cash and cash equivalents grew to $5.01 billion by July 31, 2026
findings.issue: Two different measures side by side. The sentence first gives $5.2 billion of cash and short-term investments at fiscal 2026 year-end, then says cash and cash equivalents 'grew to' $5.01 billion by July 31, 2026. A reader sees a smaller figure introduced with 'grew' and reads a contradiction or a decline; the two lines are on different bases (one includes short-term investments).
findings.fix: Name the basis difference in the sentence (the July figure is cash and cash equivalents only, the year-end figure includes short-term investments) or keep only one of the two.

findings.quote: Revenue is recognized ratably over one-to-three-year subscription terms
findings.issue: Dropped hedges. The MD&A says the agreement term 'is generally one to three years'; the overview drops 'generally'. Likewise risks.idiosyncratic[0] says 'because contracts run over a year', where the MD&A says customers 'typically sign contracts with terms over one year'.
findings.fix: Restore the source's hedges: 'generally one to three years' and 'typically run longer than a year'.

findings.quote: CrowdStrike's balance sheet is a fortress.
findings.issue: Unearned characterisation and hype. Also analystCommentary says the quarter 'was strong on every operating metric' while the same quarter carried a GAAP loss from operations of $33.2 million; 'every' is not earned.
findings.fix: Let the figures carry it (net cash of $4.5 billion against $0.7 billion of debt). In analystCommentary, say which metrics were strong (revenue, ARR, net new ARR, cash flow) instead of 'every operating metric'.

findings.quote: so fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $1.2 billion has accumulated as net cash, which reached $4.5 billion at year-end
findings.issue: Loose causal claim. It reads as though the year's free cash flow went entirely to net cash, but the Facts block shows net debt moving from -3.6 to -4.5 ($B) over fiscal 2026, a smaller change than the $1.2 billion of free cash flow, so not all of it accumulated. The $4.5 billion is the cumulative balance, not the year's accumulation.
findings.fix: Say that free cash flow, with no dividends or recorded buybacks, has built the net cash position over the five years, without tying the one-year figure to the year-end balance.
